description:
We are a team of engineering students who love bridging the gap between technical concepts and creative storytelling. Our background includes developing visual scripts for short-form animated content and designing engaging presentations.

For this hackathon, we are tackling the 'Abandoned but not Forgotten' challenge. Our goal is to create a compelling, animated short story that breathes life into the history of NASA's discarded equipment on the Moon and Mars.
summary:
Space Heritage is an interactive web-based digital museum that documents and preserves the stories of human-made spacecraft, rovers, descent stages, and scientific instruments resting on the Moon and Mars. Built using verified NASA NSSDCA catalog records, JPL imagery, and IAU planetary coordinates, the platform features a searchable 15-relic catalog, a 3D-style lunar and Martian reconnaissance map, an interactive Before & After space-weathering slider, first-person neural voice testimonials ("If This Machine Could Talk"), a complete Apollo Surface Archive, an educational quiz, and shareable collector cards.

By transforming raw mission telemetry into an accessible, human-centered experience, Space Heritage addresses the challenge of bridging space history with public STEM engagement. As humanity returns to the Moon and plans crewed Mars missions, distinguishing orbital debris from historic landing sites is vital to protecting humanity's first off-world archaeological monuments for future generations.
details:
Project Overview: What Space Heritage Does & How It Works

Space Heritage is an interactive digital museum dedicated to the human-made spacecraft, rovers, descent stages, and scientific instruments currently resting on the Moon and Mars. Rather than treating dormant off-world machinery as "space junk," the platform reframes these artifacts as monuments of human curiosity and engineering perseverance.

The web application combines historical NASA telemetry, verified NSSDCA catalog records, and interactive storytelling across seven core modules:

  • Interactive Space Museum: A searchable, filterable catalog of 15 iconic lunar and Martian relics (including Apollo 11's Eagle descent stage, Apollo 15's Lunar Roving Vehicle, Spirit, Opportunity, InSight, and Viking landers) with verified coordinates, mission timelines, and physical status documentation.
  • 3D-Style Planetary Reconnaissance Map: A zoomable, pannable coordinate map of the Moon and Mars featuring geo-referenced pulsing telemetry beacons across lunar maria and Martian basins, linking each landing site directly to its full museum record.
  • If This Machine Could Talk (First-Person Testimonials): Documentary-style narratives told from the perspective of the rovers and landers themselves, paired with Web Speech neural narration and realistic prosody pauses.
  • Before & After Historical Gallery: An interactive split-screen comparison slider allowing users to drag across decades of space weathering—comparing pristine spacecraft upon landing against orbital reconnaissance imagery and 14 years of Martian ferric oxide dust accumulation.
  • Apollo Surface Archive: Comprehensive mission chronicles of all six crewed Apollo lunar landings (1969–1972), tracking surface durations, EVA times, and the 382 kg of lunar samples returned to Earth.
  • Ten-Question Space Quiz: An educational assessment with instant verified explanations covering lunar modules, laser retroreflectors, Mars rovers, and off-world heritage preservation.
  • Shareable Story Cards: High-resolution digital collector cards with NSSDCA catalog IDs and planetary coordinates that students, educators, and space enthusiasts can generate and share.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Reframing Space Sustainability & Heritage: As humanity prepares to return to the Moon and venture toward Mars, Space Heritage highlights the critical distinction between orbital debris that requires removal and historic landing sites that warrant international archaeological preservation.
  • Accessible STEM & Space History Education: Transforms raw NASA catalog entries and coordinates into an intuitive, tactile experience for students, teachers, and general audiences—bridging engineering history with emotional storytelling.
  • Data Verification & Transparency: Every artifact, coordinate, and comparison is anchored to authentic NASA mission archives, NSSDCA identifiers, and IAU planetary nomenclature.

Creativity & Design Philosophy

  • Humanizing Robotic Explorers: By pairing mission telemetry with first-person audio stories ("If This Machine Could Talk"), the platform gives voice to silent machines like Opportunity ("My battery is low, and it's getting dark") and Eagle, turning technical specifications into deeply memorable human stories.
  • Mission-Control Aesthetic: Designed as a live telemetry console featuring real-time Earth UTC and Mars Jezero Sol clocks, Web Audio API synthesized telemetry pings, and high-contrast aerospace typography (Orbitron and JetBrains Mono) for effortless readability.

Tools, Languages & Technologies Used

  • Frontend & Language: React, TypeScript, and Vite for fast, modular single-page application performance.
  • Styling & UI: Tailwind CSS and Lucide Icons for a responsive dark-mode mission-control interface.
  • Audio & Interactivity: Browser Web Speech API (for natural neural narration) and custom Web Audio API synthesis (for subtle telemetry feedback), alongside hardware-accelerated CSS clip-path rendering and background image pre-decoding for zero-delay visual transitions.
  • Data & Hosting: NASA Image and Video Library, NASA NSSDCA Master Catalog, NASA JPL Photo-journal, Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera (LROC) imagery, IAU Planetary Nomenclature, and Vercel for global cloud deployment.

Key Factors Considered by Our Team

  • Scientific & Historical Accuracy: Cross-checking every landing coordinate, NSSDCA ID, mission duration, and hardware status against official NASA and IAU records so the platform serves as a trustworthy educational reference.
  • Performance & Smooth User Experience: Optimizing high-resolution planetary imagery with eager background pre-decoding and bounded coordinate panning so interactive sliders and maps run smoothly across both desktop and mobile devices.
  • Public Accessibility: Ensuring the entire experience runs natively in any modern web browser with zero paywalls, logins, or external hardware requirements.

Public Source Code Repository: https://github.com/irfanp70/space-heritage
